lines.text: Here's a rectangle with a shaded shape inside. Can you find its area?
lines.caption: Here's a rectangle with a shaded shape inside. Can you find its area?

lines.text: Lots of kids answer forty-eight. <short pause> But that's NOT quite right!
lines.caption: Lots of kids answer forty-eight. But that's NOT quite right!

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find the little piece they forgot.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's find the little piece they forgot.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: Rectangle ABCD is twelve by eight, and M is the midpoint of side CD.
lines.caption: Rectangle ABCD is twelve by eight, and M is the midpoint of side CD.

lines.text: The diagonal from A to C crosses the line from B to M at a point called P.
lines.caption: The diagonal from A to C crosses the line from B to M at a point called P.

lines.text: What is the area of the shaded region, APMD?
lines.caption: What is the area of the shaded region, APMD?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: Let's break it down. A is at the bottom left. Then come B, C and D, going around.
lines.caption: Let's break it down. A is at the bottom left. Then come B, C and D, going around.

lines.text: M is halfway along the top, so each half of the top side is six.
lines.caption: M is halfway along the top, so each half of the top side is six.

lines.text: The shaded shape has four corners: A, P, M and D.
lines.caption: The shaded shape has four corners: A, P, M and D.

lines.text: It isn't a rectangle or a triangle. So how can we find its area?
lines.caption: It isn't a rectangle or a triangle. So how can we find its area?

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Here's our plan: start with a bigger shape we already know.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Here's our plan: start with a bigger shape we already know.

lines.text: Triangle ACD is exactly half of the rectangle.
lines.caption: Triangle ACD is exactly half of the rectangle.

lines.text: Twelve times eight is ninety-six. Half of that is forty-eight.
lines.caption: Twelve times eight is ninety-six. Half of that is forty-eight.

lines.text: Our shaded shape is that triangle, with one small corner cut off: triangle PCM.
lines.caption: Our shaded shape is that triangle, with one small corner cut off: triangle PCM.

lines.text: Triangle PCM has a base of six. But how tall is it?
lines.caption: Triangle PCM has a base of six. But how tall is it?

lines.text: Look at the triangle below it, PAB. Its base is twelve.
lines.caption: Look at the triangle below it, PAB. Its base is twelve.

lines.text: The top and bottom sides are parallel, so the angles match. The triangles are similar!
lines.caption: The top and bottom sides are parallel, so the angles match. The triangles are similar!

lines.text: Six is half of twelve. So the top triangle is half as wide, so half as tall.
lines.caption: Six is half of twelve. So the top triangle is half as wide, so half as tall.

lines.text: Together the two heights make eight. So split eight into one part and two parts.
lines.caption: Together the two heights make eight. So split eight into one part and two parts.

lines.text: Each part is eight over three. So triangle PCM is eight over three tall.
lines.caption: Each part is eight over three. So triangle PCM is eight over three tall.

lines.text: Its area is base times height, over two.
lines.caption: Its area is base times height, over two.

lines.text: Six times eight over three is sixteen. Half of sixteen is eight.
lines.caption: Six times eight over three is sixteen. Half of sixteen is eight.

lines.text: Forty-eight minus eight is forty. <short pause> The answer is forty, choice A!
lines.caption: Forty-eight minus eight is forty. The answer is forty, choice A!

lines.text: Here's a second way. Let's cut the shaded shape from A to M.
lines.caption: Here's a second way. Let's cut the shaded shape from A to M.

lines.text: Now we have two triangles: ADM on the left, and APM on the right.
lines.caption: Now we have two triangles: ADM on the left, and APM on the right.

lines.text: Triangle ADM has legs six and eight. Six times eight is forty-eight, and half of that is twenty-four.
lines.caption: Triangle ADM has legs six and eight. Six times eight is forty-eight, and half of that is twenty-four.

lines.text: Triangle APM is part of a bigger triangle, AMC.
lines.caption: Triangle APM is part of a bigger triangle, AMC.

lines.text: That one has base six and height eight. So its area is twenty-four, too.
lines.caption: That one has base six and height eight. So its area is twenty-four, too.

lines.text: The similar triangles cut the diagonal two parts to one. So AP is two of the three equal parts.
lines.caption: The similar triangles cut the diagonal two parts to one. So AP is two of the three equal parts.

lines.text: Both triangles share the tip at M, so they have the same height.
lines.caption: Both triangles share the tip at M, so they have the same height.

lines.text: Their bases are on the diagonal, so the purple area is two of the three parts, too.
lines.caption: Their bases are on the diagonal, so the purple area is two of the three parts, too.

lines.text: Two over three times twenty-four is sixteen. And twenty-four plus sixteen is forty again!
lines.caption: Two over three times twenty-four is sixteen. And twenty-four plus sixteen is forty again!

lines.text: So when would you pick each way? Subtracting is fast when a big triangle is easy to see.
lines.caption: So when would you pick each way? Subtracting is fast when a big triangle is easy to see.

lines.text: Splitting is great when a point cuts a line into known parts.
lines.caption: Splitting is great when a point cuts a line into known parts.

lines.text: Choice C, forty-eight, is the big trap. It's all of triangle ACD. The corner was never cut off.
lines.caption: Choice C, forty-eight, is the big trap. It's all of triangle ACD. The corner was never cut off.

lines.text: Choice B, forty-four, takes away only four. That's half the small triangle. Check its area!
lines.caption: Choice B, forty-four, takes away only four. That's half the small triangle. Check its area!

lines.text: Choice E, fifty-six, is the part NOT shaded: ninety-six minus forty is fifty-six.
lines.caption: Choice E, fifty-six, is the part NOT shaded: ninety-six minus forty is fifty-six.

lines.text: Choice D, fifty-two, is too big. Our shape fits inside triangle ACD, so it's under forty-eight.
lines.caption: Choice D, fifty-two, is too big. Our shape fits inside triangle ACD, so it's under forty-eight.

lines.text: Here's a great habit: after you subtract, check which pieces are left.
lines.caption: Here's a great habit: after you subtract, check which pieces are left.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Now the rectangle is fifteen by eight.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Now the rectangle is fifteen by eight.

lines.text: Point M is on the top side, with MC equal to five. The diagonal from A to C meets BM at P.
lines.caption: Point M is on the top side, with MC equal to five. The diagonal from A to C meets BM at P.

lines.text: What is the area of the shaded region, APMD?
lines.caption: What is the area of the shaded region, APMD?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. The top base is five, and the bottom base is fifteen.
lines.caption: Let's check. The top base is five, and the bottom base is fifteen.

lines.text: So the bottom triangle is three times as wide, and three times as tall.
lines.caption: So the bottom triangle is three times as wide, and three times as tall.

lines.text: Split the height of eight into one part and three parts. Each part is two.
lines.caption: Split the height of eight into one part and three parts. Each part is two.

lines.text: So triangle PCM has base five and height two. Its area is five.
lines.caption: So triangle PCM has base five and height two. Its area is five.

lines.text: Triangle ACD is half of fifteen times eight, which is sixty. Sixty minus five is fifty-five!
lines.caption: Triangle ACD is half of fifteen times eight, which is sixty. Sixty minus five is fifty-five!

lines.text: Check by splitting: ADM is forty, and AMC is twenty.
lines.caption: Check by splitting: ADM is forty, and AMC is twenty.

lines.text: AP is three of the four equal parts of the diagonal.
lines.caption: AP is three of the four equal parts of the diagonal.

lines.text: So the purple triangle is three quarters of twenty: fifteen.
lines.caption: So the purple triangle is three quarters of twenty: fifteen.

lines.text: Forty plus fifteen is fifty-five. If you found fifty-five, amazing work!
lines.caption: Forty plus fifteen is fifty-five. If you found fifty-five, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: When two lines cross, look for similar triangles to find the crossing point.
lines.caption: When two lines cross, look for similar triangles to find the crossing point.

lines.text: Then take a big triangle, and subtract the small piece you don't want.
lines.caption: Then take a big triangle, and subtract the small piece you don't want.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
